the dataset contains 1125 games of 10 minutes each, with the following characteristics: - Each game is played by two teams (of 11 agents each) - Each game is 600 seconds long - There are 45 different team combinations - Each agent has a unique ID - Each agent has its own local percept (noisy and incomplete)
the dataset contains: (1) 45 different pairings of the 10 best teams in RoboCUP soccer simulation league (2D) from 2016 and (2017) and (2) more than 180 hrs of game play.

the dataset can be used for: - training and testing of machine learning models, e.g. for predicting robot behaviors; - evaluation of robot behaviors, e.g. to compare different robot controllers; - research on the design and analysis of robot behaviors, and their impact on team performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel machine learning methods for data analysis, data mining and knowledge discovery in this dataset.
the development of a large-scale dataset for the RoboCup simulation soccer domain.
the development of methods that can learn to predict the future from the noisy, local, and incomplete percepts that each robot has.
